items.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: One of the great stories about Federico was, when he goes to the Palladium Ballroom... who used to be the promoter that eventually went and opened up the Palladium

ctx.x: Yes. He got teachers. Then they saw that he had really a special talent, and the next thing you know, he was playing tangos, paso dobles, and doing the rumba. By 14, he’d started to play professionally in a place called the Park Plaza, which is now a church, on 112th Street... When you’re going into the park on Fifth Avenue, there’s a church there. That used to be known as the Park Plaza, and that’s the first dances that Machito and his Afro-Cubans played when a promoter called Federico Pagani, who used to be the…
